# Pedagogical Report: IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5_patched.ipynb

Generated from `IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5_patched.ipynb` on 2026-05-04 23:35 UTC.

## Instructor orientation

The notebook implements Intelligent Data Detective v5 as a LangGraph supervisor-worker workflow. At a high level, it loads a dataset, stores DataFrames in a registry, lets specialized LLM agents clean/analyze/visualize the data, packages a substantive report, writes canonical artifacts, and validates the final state. The main flow is:

```text
Supervisor → Initial Analysis → Data Cleaner → Analyst → Visualization
          → Report Orchestrator → Section Workers → Report Packager → File Writer
```

The report below is intentionally instructor-facing. For each cell, it explains the section's teaching purpose, then walks through every source line in that cell. Markdown cells are treated as narrative scaffolding; code cells are treated as executable implementation. Very large cells are still covered line by line, with repeated explanatory patterns where a long block consists of prompts, schemas, tools, or routing logic.

## How to teach from this document

- Display each notebook cell, then read the matching section below.
- Use the “Teaching purpose” paragraph to explain why the cell exists before stepping through code.
- Use the “Line-by-line walkthrough” bullets while demoing individual source lines.
- For large cells, focus students first on the detected definitions/imports, then use the line bullets as a reference manual.

## Closing teaching synthesis

The notebook is best taught as a complete production-style agent system rather than as isolated Python snippets. Early cells establish environment, types, models, and shared state. Middle cells define prompts, tools, memory, agents, and graph topology. Later cells execute, stream, inspect, persist, and validate the workflow. The central engineering lesson is that reliable AI systems depend on typed boundaries, deterministic state reducers, recoverable tool errors, explicit artifact paths, and validation gates—not only on LLM prompting.
